assertion: About one in three Texas students left college without earning a degree — and in the last five years, they accumulated $1.1 billion in student debt, a new study found.
independent_value: Report via FOX 4: 38% (347,061) left without a credential; at least $1.09B owed
inaccuracy: The claim says about one in three Texas students; the study says 38% of Texas public high school graduates who enrolled within a year, and the debt is a floor ('at least $1.09B') for the 2017-2022 cohorts.

assertion: The researchers tracked 900,000 students who enrolled in college within one year of graduating from a Texas high school between 2017 and 2022.
Within six years of enrolling, 49% had completed a credential. Meanwhile, 38% of students — or more than 300,000 students — had left school, and 14% were still enrolled.
independent_value: 49% completed; 38% = 347,061 left; shares sum to 101% from rounding
reason: Matches the report as relayed; the 101% total is rounding. Only a secondary relay of the report was read.

assertion: Most of those who left did so in the first year of college.
independent_value: 51% leave in year one; 78% by end of year two

assertion: Signs that students were academically struggling were apparent as their grade averages hovered just above 1.0
independent_value: Report: half of first-year departures left with a GPA of 1.0 or lower
inaccuracy: The article says grade averages hovered just above 1.0; the report says half of first-year departures had a GPA of 1.0 or lower, not that averages were above 1.0 or that this holds for all leavers.

windows_tested.value: not reported in the sources read

why_not: The 1.0 figure appears in the Tribune text itself, which is the article under test; the contrary evidence is FOX 4's relay of the report.

assertion: Nearly 30% of those who left college had debt with the average student loan borrower owing $6,250 with no diploma or certificate to qualify for higher paying jobs, according to the findings.
independent_value: FOX 4: median balance of $6,250 per borrower; 331,373 non-returners owe at least $1.09B
inaccuracy: The claim says the average borrower owes $6,250; the evidence says $6,250 is the median balance per borrower.
why_not: The $6,250 appears in the article under test; the contrary evidence is the report's median label as relayed by FOX 4. The 30% borrower share could not be verified.

assertion: The state saw an annual wage gap of $20,800 between those who completed college and those who did not.
warehouse_value: ACS 2024 Texas median earnings: bachelor's $70,006 vs some college/associate $46,890 (gap $23,116)
sql: SELECT year, median_earnings_some_college, median_earnings_bachelors FROM census.acs_earnings_by_education WHERE state='48' AND year IN (2023,2024)
independent_value: Report: $60,500 completers vs $39,700 non-completers, 10 years after HS
reason: Matches the report; ACS gives the same order of magnitude. Correlational, not causal.

assertion: outgoing Gov. Greg Abbott had set goals that 60% of working age adults would have completed a degree or postsecondary credential of value
independent_value: Governor's office announced 60x30 on Nov 16, 2015 (60% of ages 25-34); THECB's later plan covers ages 25-64 with credential of value
reason: The governor's office announced the 60% by 2030 goal; the working-age and credential-of-value wording is from the later coordinating board plan.
